_comment: The release label for the whole toolkit. Bump it deliberately when you
publish; build_manifest.py stamps it into manifest.json and every
artifact URL, and publish.py uses it as the bucket directory.
Deliberately NOT derived from a git tag: distribution is bucket +
manifest (and native .exe/.dmg installers), not GitHub releases, so the
release label is ours to set rather than something git hands us.

Remember: this label is for humans and changelogs. Whether a package

_discovery_comment: These two ride into the DISCOVERY document, not the manifest -- they are
the only two levers that reach an install whose endpoint has moved or
minimum_updater: the oldest FNS_Updater Pkgversion still allowed to run.
Empty means no floor, which is the normal state. Raise it ONLY when a
shipped updater is genuinely dangerous: every install below the floor
stops updating and tells the user why. It cannot be undone for anyone
who is offline, so treat it as a recall, not a nudge.
notices: short messages every install sees. Keep them few and true.
_retired_comment: Packages this release DELIBERATELY no longer ships. publish.py refuses
to stage a release that drops a package the previous one published
unless the name is listed here -- the manifest is regenerated wholesale
from the live project, so an unloaded package would otherwise vanish
silently and every install would stop being offered it.
The four below are the 3.0 redesign's renames and dissolutions, which
happened before the guard existed: FNS_Config -> FNS_ConfigRegistry (+
FNS_Updater, and tools_ui dissolved into FNS_Hub. They are declared
here because they are genuinely gone, not because the guard is noisy.
Prune a name once no published manifest still lists it: a stale entry
pre-authorises a future accidental drop. Stage() reports stale entries.
QuickParCustom (folded into CustomParTools) retired in the v3.0.x
cycle -- declared 2026-08-28 ahead of the first v3 Stage(), which
would otherwise refuse them as undeclared drops.
